definitions.gloss: personal motto; favorite maxim; guiding principle
definitions.explanation: A phrase, proverb, or saying that a person keeps in mind as a guiding principle in life. Literally 'inscription at one's right side.'

examples.japanese: あなたの{座右|ざゆう}の{銘|めい}は{何|なん}ですか。
{座右|ざゆう}の{銘|めい}は「{継続|けいぞく}は{力|ちから}なり」です。
{面接|めんせつ}で{座右|ざゆう}の{銘|めい}を{聞|き}かれることがあるので、{準備|じゅんび}しておくといい。
examples.english: You may be asked about your personal motto in an interview, so it's good to prepare one.

notes:
Literally means "inscription at one's right side," referring to the ancient Chinese practice of keeping a guiding inscription on the right side of one's desk. {座右|ざゆう} means "at one's side" and {銘|めい} means "inscription" or "engraved words."

USAGE:
This is a very common question in Japanese self-introductions, job interviews, and school profiles. People typically choose a proverb, a famous quote, or a personal principle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {座右|ざゆう}の{銘|めい}にする: to adopt as one's motto
- {座右|ざゆう}の{銘|めい}は〜です: my motto is...
- {座右|ざゆう}の{銘|めい}を{聞|き}く: to ask someone's motto

SIMILAR WORDS:
- モットー: motto — loanword from English, more casual
- {信条|しんじょう}: creed, belief — broader, refers to a set of beliefs or principles
- {教訓|きょうくん}: lesson, moral — focuses on a lesson learned from experience
